Plot feature abundance over time

Source: R/plot_trend.R
plot_trend.Rd

Plot trend of feature abundances / expression over time by mean and standard deviation (SD) for each group. Accepts either a SummarizedExperiment object (computing mean/SD internally via calc_mean_sd()), a pre-computed table from calc_mean_sd(), or a named list of SummarizedExperiment objects (multiple datasets, e.g. multiomics).

Usage

plot_trend(
  se_obj,
  assay = 1,
  groups = NULL,
  features,
  title = NULL,
  ylabel = "Log2 abundance",
  errorbar = TRUE,
  fontsize = 8,
  multi_layout = c("wrap", "vertical", "horizontal", "overlay"),
  ncol = NULL,
  independent_y = TRUE
)

Arguments

se_obj

A SummarizedExperiment object, a data.frame from calc_mean_sd() with columns: Feature, Time, Group, Mean, SD, or a named list of SummarizedExperiment objects (multiple datasets, e.g. multiomics).

assay

The assay to use in the SummarizedExperiment object: a numeric index or character name, e.g. 1 or "orig" for original data, 2 or "norm" for time 0 normalised data. (Default: 1.)

groups

Groups to be plotted, if NULL, all groups will be used (default is NULL)

features

Features to be plotted, if NULL, an error will be raised

title

Title of the plot. "Feature" if NULL (default) for single input, "Trends across datasets" if NULL for a named list of SummarizedExperiment objects.

ylabel

Y axis label of the plot (default is "Log2 abundance").

errorbar

Whether to plot error bars (default is TRUE)

fontsize

Font size for the plot (default is 8)

multi_layout

Facet layout for multiple-datasets input: "wrap" (default): wraps features, datasets nested per feature; "vertical": datasets as rows, features as columns; "horizontal": features as rows, datasets as columns; "overlay": one panel per feature, datasets by linetype. Ignored for single input.

ncol

Number of feature columns per row for "wrap" and "overlay" layouts (multiple datasets) or in facet_wrap() (single input). If NULL (default), auto-computed.

independent_y

If TRUE (default), each panel gets its own y-axis scale. If FALSE, y-axes are shared: within each facet row for "vertical" and "horizontal" layouts, fully for "wrap" and "overlay".

Value

Plot of feature abundances over time by mean and SD

Examples

data(example_obj)
data(example_obj_2)
plot_trend(example_obj,
    features = sample(rownames(example_obj), 4))
#> Group not specified. Plotting all groups: IFNbeta, IFNgamma, LPS, untreated


# Also accepts a named list of SummarizedExperiment objects
plot_trend(list(Exp1 = example_obj, Exp2 = example_obj_2),
    features = sample(rownames(example_obj), 2))
#> Group not specified. Plotting all groups: IFNbeta, IFNgamma, LPS, untreated
